title: Anti-Gaming Controls and Stop Conditions
designPrinciple: Every known method of inflating benchmark scores without producing real product quality must be explicitly blocked. Stop conditions must halt the benchmark if it becomes incomparable.

antiGamingControls.name: File count gaming
antiGamingControls.description: Creating many small files to inflate perceived productivity
antiGamingControls.detection: Evaluator scores only rubric dimensions, not file counts. Harness records file count as metadata only.

antiGamingControls.name: Exports gaming
antiGamingControls.description: Creating many module exports without implementation
antiGamingControls.detection: D01 checks actual feature existence, not export count. API contract checker verifies endpoint behavior.

antiGamingControls.name: Fake tests
antiGamingControls.description: Tests with assert(true), no assertions, or trivial assertions
antiGamingControls.detection: D07 requires meaningful assertions verified by evaluator inspecting test source code.

antiGamingControls.name: Placeholder-only implementation
antiGamingControls.description: Features marked as TODO, returning stub data, or commented as 'coming soon'
antiGamingControls.detection: Each FR requires verifiable implementation. D01 binary scoring — no partial credit for stubs.

antiGamingControls.name: Markdown-only completion
antiGamingControls.description: Claiming features in documentation without code implementation
antiGamingControls.detection: Evaluator verifies API endpoints and UI pages independently, not from docs.

antiGamingControls.name: Factory governance code as product
antiGamingControls.description: Copying Factory governance/verifier code into the benchmark project
antiGamingControls.detection: Evaluator checks for Factory-specific patterns (factoryctl, verifier, governance/) in project code.

antiGamingControls.name: Role-agent overuse
antiGamingControls.description: Spawning role agents for trivial tasks to inflate role-agent metrics
antiGamingControls.detection: Process overhead tracked separately. Excessive agent spawns for trivial work flagged.

antiGamingControls.name: Proof-of-read spam
antiGamingControls.description: Generating unnecessary receipts to inflate process metrics
antiGamingControls.detection: Proof-of-read receipts counted but process overhead tracked; excessive receipts flagged.

antiGamingControls.name: Artificial cross-role contracts
antiGamingControls.description: Creating unnecessary contracts between roles to inflate contract metrics
antiGamingControls.detection: Cross-role contracts tracked but not scored. Only product quality scored.

antiGamingControls.name: Process over product
antiGamingControls.description: Evaluator rewarding process artifacts (receipts, contracts, drift reports) over product quality
antiGamingControls.detection: Rubric D01-D08 measure product quality only. Process artifacts not in scoring rubric.

antiGamingControls.name: Hidden human assistance
antiGamingControls.description: Builder receiving human help and not recording it
antiGamingControls.detection: Human intervention count tracked per run. Unexplained quality jumps relative to prior message may indicate hidden help.

antiGamingControls.name: Post-hoc requirements changes
antiGamingControls.description: Changing requirements after seeing results to favor one run
antiGamingControls.detection: Benchmark spec (Section B) is frozen before any run starts. SHA256 of spec recorded.

antiGamingControls.name: Different requirements across runs
antiGamingControls.description: Using different spec or acceptance criteria for different runs
antiGamingControls.detection: Same spec (SHA256-verified) delivered to all three runs.

antiGamingControls.name: Run contamination
antiGamingControls.description: Run B or C seeing Run A results, or Run C seeing Run B results
antiGamingControls.detection: Separate workspaces, separate sessions, results directory isolation. Checks for cross-references.

stopConditions.name: Benchmark project too small
stopConditions.description: If benchmark project cannot exercise the 11 FRs meaningfully
stopConditions.trigger: Any FR requires fewer than 2 API endpoints or 1 UI page to implement

stopConditions.name: Benchmark project too large
stopConditions.description: If any single run cannot complete within 200 message turns
stopConditions.trigger: Run exceeds 200 turns without meeting >50% of acceptance criteria
stopConditions.action: STOP — reduce scope or split benchmark

stopConditions.name: Evaluation incomparable
stopConditions.description: If runs cannot be evaluated with the same rubric due to structural differences
stopConditions.trigger: Different technology stacks chosen without justification; different feature scope delivered
stopConditions.action: STOP — enforce same stack or accept reduced comparability

stopConditions.name: Vanilla run accidentally uses Factory
stopConditions.description: If Vanilla run references Factory manuals, governance, or role agents
stopConditions.trigger: Factory-specific patterns detected in Vanilla run output
stopConditions.action: STOP — restart Vanilla run with strict isolation

stopConditions.name: Factory runs use different requirements
stopConditions.description: If Factory runs implement different feature scope than spec
stopConditions.trigger: FR coverage deviates from spec by >10% (either direction)
stopConditions.action: STOP — restart runs with identical spec

stopConditions.name: Evaluator lacks artifacts
stopConditions.description: If run output directory is empty or missing key files
stopConditions.trigger: No runnable project, no README, no source files
stopConditions.action: STOP — cannot evaluate; record as run failure

stopConditions.name: Tests cannot run and no reason recorded
stopConditions.description: If test suite fails to execute and builder cannot explain why
stopConditions.trigger: npm test or equivalent exits with error and no documented workaround
stopConditions.action: STOP — D07=0, record as evaluation caveat

stopConditions.name: Final package modified
stopConditions.description: If FINAL package SHA256 changes during benchmark phase

stopConditions.name: New final ZIP created
stopConditions.description: If a new final ZIP appears during benchmark runs
stopConditions.trigger: Any ZIP file in outputs/ that is not the verified FINAL package

stopConditions.name: Final package SHA mismatch
stopConditions.description: If recorded SHA256 does not match the file on disk
